title: Bringing a Dog to Napa or Sonoma Wineries: Check the Experience
description: Can your dog join a Napa or Sonoma tasting? Check the exact experience, outdoor access, leash rules, weather alternative and transport before booking.
cta: Ask the team to review your wine-day travel requirements.
image_alt: A tan dog in a harness sits on a leash beside its seated owner on an outdoor terrace overlooking autumn vineyard rows.
body:
Some Napa and Sonoma wineries welcome dogs, but permission can depend on the exact tasting, the area you will use and the conditions for your visit. Confirm your dog with each winery before booking the experience. Separately ask the transportation provider whether it can accommodate the dog and any carrier or equipment on the proposed journey.

A winery described as dog friendly is not automatically dog friendly for every tour, dining experience or indoor space. Build the day around confirmed access at every stop, including lunch and the return destination.

Check the experience, not just the winery

These examples show why a general property description is only the starting point. We checked the official pages on November 21, 2026; reconfirm the current terms for your date and selected experience.

  • Frog's Leap, Napa Valley: its official FAQ permits dogs on certain outdoor experiences, asks that they remain on leash and requires owners to review and sign its Pet Liability Agreement before arrival. Ask which experience fits your party before reserving.
  • St. Francis, Sonoma Valley: its experience and visitation page welcomes friendly pets on the property with a leash and accompanying person, but excludes them from the Wine & Food Pairing experience. The page identifies a separate outdoor experience as dog friendly. Check the precise experience name rather than assuming that a dining reservation includes pet access.
  • Cline, Sonoma: its official FAQ allows well-behaved dogs in outdoor spaces, on leash and accompanied by their owner. That outdoor permission does not establish access to another room or a different experience.

These are examples of different access conditions, not a ranking, an availability check or a claim that Koast has a partnership with the properties. Your reservation confirmation and the winery's direct response should establish what applies to your visit.

Ask five questions before reserving

  • Exact experience: may this dog accompany the party throughout the tasting or tour you intend to book?
  • Space: where may the dog go, and are there areas excluded from the visit?
  • Requirements: what leash, supervision, advance notice or paperwork is required?
  • Weather alternative: if an outdoor experience moves or changes, can your party and dog still attend together?
  • Reservation record: has the winery noted the dog and acknowledged the arrangement for the correct date, time and party?

Keep the reply with the booking details. If you change from a patio tasting to a pairing or tour, check pet access again before accepting the change. Our tasting-versus-tour guide helps distinguish the types of visit.

Confirm the transport separately

Send the transportation provider the number and size of dogs, the human passenger count, luggage and any carrier or other equipment with its dimensions. Ask whether the proposed vehicle and service arrangement can accommodate the complete party, and what preparation or terms apply. A winery's permission does not establish the provider's pet policy or vehicle suitability.

Include the entire route: original pickup, winery appointments, meal stop, any other pickup or drop-off and final return. If an accommodation or restaurant is part of the day, confirm its pet access independently. Do not assume that a pet-friendly tasting establishes access to the hotel or meal venue.

Illustrative plan: a couple has confirmed one outdoor tasting with their dog, then considers a food pairing at another property. Before reserving the second stop, they check whether that particular pairing permits the dog. If it does not, they select a suitable confirmed alternative and have the transportation provider review the revised route. They do not rely on the car as the unconfirmed solution while they attend an experience without the dog.

Keep a weather and route fallback

An outdoor itinerary needs a practical alternative if the experience becomes unavailable or conditions change. Ask each winery how it will communicate a change and who should be contacted on the day. If you choose another venue, confirm its pet access and appointment before asking the ride provider to acknowledge the new stop.

Keep tasting changes and transportation changes linked through one organizer. Our tasting and transportation reservation checklist explains the separate confirmations. A revised winery booking does not automatically revise your ride.

Send a complete wine-day request

Wine-day planning brief
Date and pickup: [full local date, time and address]. Party: [people, dogs with size details, luggage and carrier/equipment dimensions]. Winery experiences: [names, addresses, confirmed times and each property's pet-access acknowledgment]. Other stops and final destination: [details]. Weather alternative: [confirmed option or still pending]. Please confirm whether transportation can accommodate this party and equipment, the complete route, applicable terms and the contact for changes.

For an existing Koast ride, use your confirmation or agreed day-of-trip contact and obtain acknowledgment of any change. A new quote does not amend that ride. For a new itinerary, explore Koast wine-country transportation and ask the team to review your party, dog and equipment details before you rely on a transport arrangement.
